findings.what: The condition is inverted: `disarm_settings_candidate` returns true when it cancelled an armed candidate, so the cursor now moves only right after a cancel (the old code never moved then) and never moves when nothing is armed, which breaks normal Up/Down/First/Last navigation in settings; it needs `!self.disarm_settings_candidate()`, and the updated test `movement_cancels_an_armed_candidate_rather_than_also_moving` would fail on its cursor assertion.
